text: {"final": {"verdict": "accept", "reason": "Verified against the code: sent_messages() returns SmsMessage objects with id/household_id/template_id/params attributes; delivery_status() reads data/sms_status.json mapping SMS ids to 'delivered'/'failed' (missing for new messages), so filtering on statuses.get(m.id) == 'failed' texts exactly the failed households and skips delivered/missing ones. queue_sms(household_id, template_id, params) checks the household's sms_ok flag, re-renders the same approved template with the same params, uses the household's registered phone, and appends a new line to outbox/sms.jsonl with a fresh SMS id (next_number/format_sms_id) and new queued_at — matching the item's description. store.append_jsonl('audit.jsonl', ...) exists and appends only; nothing edits or deletes outbox lines. The script follows the scripts/stock_report.py pattern (sys.path.insert then imports), and the docstring states it sends SMS as required. config.settings does export now (sms.py imports it from there). One queue_sms call per failed message means exactly one new text per failed household when run once."}}
reasoning:
Check config.settings has `now`. The sms module imports `from config.settings import now as _now`, so `now` exists in config.settings. Also `feature` exists. The script imports `from config.settings import now` — fine.

Check store.append_jsonl("audit.jsonl", ...) — matches pattern. Audit entry fields: event, actor, ref, at — plausible.

queue_sms checks sms_ok, renders template, appends to outbox with fresh id via next_number/format_sms_id. Yes.

One concern: queue_sms raises ValueError if household.sms_ok is False — script would crash mid-run. But that's arguably correct behavior; the ticket says resend to same household. Not a bug per se; the item's description says "this checks the household's sms_ok flag" — accurate.

Another concern: statuses.get(m.id) != "failed" skips delivered and missing — correct per ticket.

Does the script re-send exactly once per failed message? Yes, one queue_sms per failed message. If run once, fine.

Docstring states it sends SMS — yes.

Everything checks out. Accept.
